title: Emergency Residency Switch and Authorization Fallback Playbook
author: Priya Patel
content:
Overview:
This playbook describes the one-hour emergency pattern for switching active data residency and activating an authorization fallback policy when a region, vendor, or legal requirement forces immediate data locality changes. It combines incident response steps, RBAC adjustments, audit logging requirements, evidence packaging rules, and secure-SDLC gating to ensure compliance and minimal customer impact.

When to use:
- Regulatory or legal instruction to stop processing in a region (court order, blocking by regulator).
- Infrastructure emergency (major cloud outage, region compromise).
- Discovery of residency leak tied to a specific compute region or storage cluster.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Switch active residency control-plane to an approved alternate region within 60 minutes.
- Ensure all authorization decisions for affected tenants follow a defined fallback policy that enforces least privilege and explicit allow-lists.
- Produce a complete compliance evidence bundle within 24 hours for legal / audit review.
- Maintain SLOs for availability TBA: aim to keep API latency degradation to <2x baseline for core read operations.

Scope and exclusions:
- Applies to Redwood-hosted inference control plane and customer data paths managed by Redwood Private and Dedicated services.
- Excludes customer-managed on-prem deployments (see private-deployment owner runbooks).

Key definitions:
- Active residency: the region/storage location currently serving persisted customer data for a tenant.
- Residency switch: the operational act of redirecting new writes and rekeying metadata to a target region and sequestering the source region.
- Authorization fallback policy: temporary global RBAC policy that limits cross-region privileges and requires explicit approvals for elevated actions.

Ownership and escalation:
- Incident lead (security oncall): single point of coordination.
- Cloud ops lead: performs cloud network/workload changes and validates failover.
- Platform infra lead: coordinates traffic routing, DNS, and control-plane switches.
- Legal & compliance liaison: validates evidence and approves notifications.
- Customer Success escalation manager: owns customer comms templates and QBR followups.

Checklist: pre-incident readiness (quarterly):
- Run a simulated residency switch playbook in game-day (owner: eng-sre).
- Maintain canonical list of approved target-residencies and KMS endpoints (owner: eng-private-deployments).
- Ensure audit exporter and immutable store have cross-region replication enabled for evidence (owner: eng-platform).

Emergency procedure (step-by-step):
1) Triage & decision (0–10 minutes)
   1.1 Confirm scope: affected tenants, services, and regions.
   1.2 Incident lead triggers "Residency Switch" incident type in the status page and notifies stakeholder list.
   1.3 Legal liaison provides immediate guidance on retention/notification windows.

2) Lock down and snapshot (10–25 minutes)
   2.1 Place read-only FLAGS on source storage clusters (CLI example):
       # AWS example - snapshot and set immutable flag
       aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket redwood-tenant-xyz --versioning-configuration Status=Suspended
       aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --description "residency-lock-2027-03-10"
   2.2 Trigger immediate audit export of authentication and authorization logs for the last 72 hours to the immutable evidence store.
   2.3 Generate a signed manifest that enumerates the snapshot IDs, producers, and timelines.

3) Activate authorization fallback (25–40 minutes)
   3.1 Push temporary RBAC policy: fallback policies are centrally stored as declarative YAML in the authz service. Example snippet (apply via control-plane CLI):
       # fallback-policy.yaml (string)
       policy_name: residency-fallback-2027-03-10
       description: Emergency fallback restricting sensitive actions until residency stabilized
       rules:
         - subject: role:admin
           resources: [control-plane:write, key-management:rotate]
           effect: deny
         - subject: role:support
           resources: [billing:read, metrics:read]
           effect: allow
       enforcement_mode: strict
   3.2 Verify policy application with smoke queries against the authz API:
       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://authz.internal/api/v1/validate?subject=service-x&resource=control-plane:write
   3.3 Incrementally enable explicit allow requests via support workflow (2‑person approval).

4) Change residency routing (40–60 minutes)
   4.1 Update control-plane feature flag to switch read/write traffic for affected tenants to target region. Feature flag example (LaunchDarkly / internal flags):
       redwood.flags.set("tenant.xyz.active_residency", "eu-west-2")
   4.2 Re-issue per-tenant encryption keys bound to the new KMS endpoint; rotate ephemeral signing keys.
   4.3 Run consistency checks: sample 100 objects per tenant, compare checksums and metadata timestamps.

5) Evidence packaging and communications (30–24h)
   5.1 Produce evidence bundle: snapshots, signed manifests, authz-policy diff, audit logs, DNS changes, and operator runbooks. Evidence format: a gzipped tar with a manifest.json (signed).
   5.2 Notify impacted customers with templated emails (customer success) and provide access to status pages. Do not include raw logs containing PII unless customer-specific legal approval obtained.

Audit logging & evidence rules (must-haves):
- All RBAC policy changes must be logged with actor, timestamp, diff, and reason.
- Audit export must include authentication events, authorization decisions, key-management operations, and storage ACL changes.
- Evidence retention class: emergency bundles stored in immutable archive for 7 years (or longer if legal dictates).
- Chain-of-custody: every evidence bundle receives HSM-backed signing (owner: security).

Evidence checklist (fields required in manifest):
| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| incident_id | generated incident UUID | inc-2027-00041 |
| snapshot_ids | list of storage snapshot identifiers | [snap-01, snap-02] |
| applied_policies | RBAC policy artifact names and checksums | residency-fallback-2027-03-10:sha256:... |
| audit_log_range | timestamps covered | 2027-03-07T00:00:00Z -> 2027-03-10T10:00:00Z |
| signed_by | operator identity and signature | priya.patel@redwood (sig:...) |

Post-incident activities (24h–90d):
- 24–72h: Forensic review by security + legal; confirm no PII leak and finalize evidence bundle.
- 7d: Begin phased rollback of fallback policy if verified stabilization and legal signoff. Rollback requires: unit tests, integration smoke-tests, signed approval from legal and incident lead.
- 30–90d: Incorporate lessons learned into SDLC gates: require automated residency-change tests and policy-simulation in CI (owner: eng-devex).

Testing and simulation guidance:
- Run quarterly simulation with synthetic tenants and an isolated target region. Validate that: policy application completes in <15 minutes; routing switch completes in <45 minutes; and evidence bundle can be assembled within 6 hours.
- CI jobs should include a residency switch smoke test that exercises KMS rotations and checksum validations.

Related controls and links:
- See: security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/least-privilege-evidence-and-access-risk-playbook (for RBAC hardening patterns)
- See: security-and-compliance/audit-logging/immutable-audit-store-design-evidence-catalog (for audit architecture)
- Ticket templates: /ops/templates/residency-switch-notice.md

Appendix: emergency CLI helpers and sample commands (do not run outside incident context):
- Force export of authz decisions (internal):
  curl -X POST https://authz.internal/api/v1/export -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXPORT_TOKEN" -d '{"since":"2027-03-07T00:00:00Z","bucket":"evidence-immutable"}'

- Apply fallback policy via control-plane:
  REDWOOD_CP_TOKEN=$ADMIN_TOKEN redwoodctl apply-policy --file fallback-policy.yaml --reason "residency emergency"

- Evidence signing (example):
  aws s3 cp evidence-bundle.tar.gz s3://evidence-immutable/inc-2027-00041/
  aws kms sign --key-id arn:aws:kms:.. --message fileb://manifest.json --signature fileb://manifest.sig

Approval and governance:
- Any rollback of the fallback policy requires: incident lead signoff, legal signoff, and an automated test run that includes a residency smoke test.
- All policy artifacts used in emergency mode must be archived and added to the quarterly compliance evidence review.

Contact and escalation directory:

- Legal emergency: legal-emergency@redwood.com
